summary.headline: Fair value Rs 448: the non-voting share at Rs 346.25 is a buy; the voting share at Rs 399.75 is fair, buy it at Rs 381 or lower
summary.text: Hatton National Bank (HNB.N0000 voting, HNB.X0000 non-voting) is one of Sri Lanka's strongest private banks, and it is growing fast: loans up 20.7% in nine months, net interest income up 24% and fees up 25%. But profit hasn't followed, because provisions are a charge again (Rs 6.6bn for the group, against a Rs 6.9bn write-back a year earlier): group profit for the nine months to September 2026 fell 3% to Rs 32.4bn (EPS Rs 56.11), and group return on equity is about 13.9% (bank 15.7%). I now value it at about Rs 448 a share (Rs 351 before). Most of the rise comes from the house cost of equity of 16.5% (beta 0.80), which replaces the 18% I set by hand; the rest from a higher NAV (Rs 554.63). I cut the long-run ROE a point to 13 / 15 / 17%. Buy price Rs 381, strong buy Rs 336. The voting share at Rs 399.75 is about 11% below fair value but above the buy price. The non-voting share at Rs 346.25 has the same dividends and profit share, sits below the buy price and only 3% above the strong-buy price: that is the one to buy. Watch capital: CET1 fell to 14.26% from 16.85% as loans grew.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of the four methods 30/50/20 (Rs 448.1, about 0.81x group NAV). It applies to both share classes, which have the same rights to profit and dividends.

highlights.title: Nine months to September 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Group profit attributable fell 3.2% to Rs 32.4bn and group EPS to Rs 56.11 from Rs 57.99; Q3 down 4.6%. The bank alone earned Rs 33.0bn, up 4.8%.

highlights.title: Strong growth, eaten by provisions
highlights.text: Bank net interest income rose 23.6% (margin 4.50%) and fees 25.4%. Impairment was a Rs 5.3bn charge at the bank against a Rs 7.5bn write-back a year earlier, so group pre-tax profit was flat. A Q3 trading loss of Rs 8.8bn was largely offset by exchange gains in other income.

highlights.title: Loans and asset quality
highlights.text: Gross loans up Rs 313.5bn (20.7%) to Rs 1.83tn in nine months; deposits up 12.8% to Rs 2.21tn. Net Stage 3 steady at 1.09%, coverage 73.5%.

highlights.title: Capital is tightening
highlights.text: CET1 fell to 14.26% from 16.85% and total capital to 16.59% (minimum 13.5%) after the loan growth and Rs 8.1bn of subordinated debt repaid. Liquidity coverage 165%. The 2025 dividend was paid partly in shares (Rs 5 of Rs 20).

methodReadings.reading: Group NAV per share at 30 September 2026 (bank Rs 500.83). The voting share is at 0.72x and the non-voting at 0.62x, so both pass your NAV rule.
Nine months of 2026, annualised. Group 16.9% in 2025 and 18.4% in 2024, helped by provision write-backs; 11.5% in 2023.
On trailing group EPS of Rs 81.35. Year-end P/E 2.8–4.8x in 2021–2025.
Rs 20 for 2025: Rs 15 cash and Rs 5 in new shares. Cash alone is 3.8% (4.3% on the non-voting share).
Cost of equity from beta 0.80 (provisional); 18.0% bear, 15.0% bull.
Total capital 16.59% against a 13.5% minimum, down from 19.95% as loans grew 21%.
Gross 4.12% (4.56% at end-2025), 73.5% covered by provisions.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: (Long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth) × group NAV Rs 554.63: 0.62x / 0.86x / 1.25x book, with ROE 13% / 15% / 17% and growth 5% / 6% / 7%.

models.name: P/E method
models.comment: 2027 group EPS Rs 74 / 84 / 92 × 4.5 / 5.5 / 6.5. Base is about the Rs 81–83 run-rate plus 2027 growth; the bear case is 9–11% below it because the trailing figure includes Q4 2025's provision write-back. P/Es are a little above the 2.8–4.8x year-ends of 2021–2025 and below the justified 5.0x / 6.1x / 7.9x.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: 24% of EPS paid (as for 2025, counting the scrip) for five years while profit grows 6% / 9% / 12% (supported 12.8%), then the payout rises to 1 − growth ÷ ROE (62% / 60% / 59%) at 5% / 6% / 7% growth. The cash dividend alone (Rs 15) would give less.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF, which doesn't suit a bank. Book Rs 554.63 plus profit above the cost of equity: group ROE 13% flat / 14.5%→15% / 16%→17% over ten years, 24% payout, then the excess return grows at the long-run rate.

modelsNote: A bank's cash flows are mostly lending and deposits, so instead of a cash-flow DCF I used residual income and a justified price-to-book, alongside P/E and dividends, all at the 16.5% cost of equity (18.0% / 15.0% bear / bull). Growth check: assumed 6% / 9% / 12% a year for the next five years against 12.8% supported (76% of profit kept × 16.9% group ROE in 2025); all within 2 points. Long-run growth 5–7% stays below the 12.24% bond yield and needs 38–41% of profit kept.

scenarios.common: Cost of equity from the house formula (risk-free 8.24% + beta 0.80 × 10.28% equity premium). 2026 group EPS about Rs 77 (Rs 56.11 for nine months); 2027 assumes loans keep growing and provisions stay at a normal charge. Per-share figures use 577.32mn shares (voting and non-voting together).

sensitivity.title: Residual income base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: The voting share's Rs 399.75 is near a 16.5% cost of equity with ROE settling at 14%; at the old 18% cost of equity the base case would be about Rs 359.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 180,600 in total. The prices apply to either share class; the non-voting share already meets the first two tiers.
buyPlan.realism: The non-voting share at Rs 346.25 is below the first two tiers; the third needs a 3% fall, and it traded at Rs 314.50 in Q3 2026 (2026 range Rs 314.50–404.00). The voting share at Rs 399.75 needs about 5% for the first tier (2026 low Rs 377.00) and 16% for the strong-buy price, which it hasn't reached this year.

higher: Group ROE back above 15% with provisions at a normal level.
Q4 2026 results showing group profit growing again.
The net interest margin holding near 4.5% while loans keep growing.
A larger cash dividend (more than Rs 15) for 2026.
Lower interest rates, which would lower the cost of equity.
lower: The 20% loan growth of 2026 turning into bad loans in 2027–2028.
Capital falling further (total capital 16.59% against 13.5%), leading to more scrip dividends or a rights issue.
More trading losses not offset by exchange gains.
Deposit costs rising faster than loan rates.

quality.reason: Still a good bank, but thinner on two tests: ROE is near the 15% line and capital headroom is shrinking.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: Bank 15.7% for 9M 2026 (annualised), 18.1% in 2025, 19.9% in 2024; group 13.9%, 16.9%, 18.4%. 9–12% in 2021–2023. A borderline pass: it fails if the group stays under 15% for 2026.

tests.label: Net debt no more than equity
tests.note: A bank, so judged on capital: CET1 14.26% (minimum 8.0%), total capital 16.59% (minimum 13.5%), leverage 6.97%. Down from 16.85% / 19.95% at end-2025 as loans grew 21%.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: Profit in every year of the ten-year record, including the 2022 crisis. 2024–2025 were lifted by write-backs; 2026 shows the normal level, about Rs 77 of EPS.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Rs 15 cash plus Rs 5 in shares for 2025 (Rs 8.5bn paid in cash in 2026); a bank keeps most profit to fund loans.

requiredReturn.betaBasis: Provisional. A bank, so the sector's levered beta is used without relevering: Damodaran's January 2026 Bank (Money Center) beta 0.70 (web-search extract; his site couldn't be opened), against a median local beta of 0.80 (StockAnalysis 0.65 five-year, TradingView 0.80, Simply Wall St 0.84; windows of the last two not stated). The higher, 0.80, is used. Refresh in January 2027.
sources: Default spread 4.0%: market-based, Sri Lanka dollar bonds vs US Treasuries (14 Nov 2026)
Mature-market premium 4.2% and volatility factor 1.52: Damodaran, Country Risk, July 2026
Beta: web-search extracts of Damodaran's sector betas (January 2026), StockAnalysis, TradingView and Simply Wall St (16 Nov 2026)
requiredReturn.note: Cost of equity = 8.24% + 0.80 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 16.5%; bear +1.5, bull −1.5 points. No WACC: a bank's debt is its raw material, so it is valued on equity (P/B, P/E, dividends, residual income).

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2025 annual report and the 2026 interim reports. The interim figures are unaudited, and the price is from 2026-11-16 (CSE closing price), so check it before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

fullText:
Summary: Hatton National Bank (HNB.N0000 voting, HNB.X0000 non-voting) is one of Sri Lanka's strongest private banks, and it is growing fast: loans up 20.7% in nine months, net interest income up 24% and fees up 25%. But profit hasn't followed, because provisions are a charge again (Rs 6.6bn for the group, against a Rs 6.9bn write-back a year earlier): group profit for the nine months to September 2026 fell 3% to Rs 32.4bn (EPS Rs 56.11), and group return on equity is about 13.9% (bank 15.7%). I now value it at about Rs 448 a share (Rs 351 before). Most of the rise comes from the house cost of equity of 16.5% (beta 0.80), which replaces the 18% I set by hand; the rest from a higher NAV (Rs 554.63). I cut the long-run ROE a point to 13 / 15 / 17%. Buy price Rs 381, strong buy Rs 336. The voting share at Rs 399.75 is about 11% below fair value but above the buy price. The non-voting share at Rs 346.25 has the same dividends and profit share, sits below the buy price and only 3% above the strong-buy price: that is the one to buy. Watch capital: CET1 fell to 14.26% from 16.85% as loans grew.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 399.75 voting and Rs 346.25 non-voting (CSE close, 16 November 2026). On 30 September 2026 they closed at Rs 384.00 and Rs 327.00. 2026 range to September: voting Rs 377.00–460.00, non-voting Rs 314.50–404.00.
Nine months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): group profit attributable Rs 32.4bn, down 3.2%; group EPS Rs 56.11 against Rs 57.99. Q3 alone Rs 10.5bn (EPS Rs 18.24), down 4.6%. The bank alone earned Rs 33.0bn, up 4.8%.
What drove it: bank net interest income up 23.6% to Rs 85.5bn (margin 4.50% against 4.26% for 2025), net fees up 25.4% to Rs 20.6bn, total operating income up 23% to Rs 112.7bn. Q3 showed an Rs 8.8bn trading loss at the bank, offset by Rs 7.3bn of other operating income (mostly exchange gains), so read the two together. Costs up 13.6%; cost to income 36.1%. Against that, impairment was a Rs 5.3bn charge at the bank (group Rs 6.6bn), against a Rs 7.5bn write-back a year earlier: that swing of about Rs 13bn is why profit is flat while the business grows. Group pre-tax profit was flat (−0.2%).
Balance sheet: gross loans Rs 1.83tn, up Rs 313.5bn (20.7%) since December; deposits Rs 2.21tn, up 12.8%; CASA 32.0%. Net Stage 3 1.09% (gross 4.12%, coverage 73.5%). CET1 14.26% (16.85% at end-2025), total capital 16.59% against a 13.5% minimum; Rs 8.1bn of subordinated debt was repaid. Liquidity coverage 165% (228% at end-2025).
Track record (group): EPS Rs 33.27 (2021), 26.81 (2022), 39.82 (2023), 76.14 (2024), 83.23 (2025), adjusted for the share count. Group ROE 11.5% (2023), 18.4% (2024), 16.9% (2025); bank ROE 12.1%, 9.0%, 11.8%, 19.9%, 18.1% for 2021–2025. 2024–2025 were lifted by provision write-backs (Rs 78bn in 2024, partly offset by a Rs 49.5bn loss on the sovereign bond exchange; Rs 8.4bn in 2025).
Dividends: Rs 20 for 2025 (Rs 15 cash, Rs 5 scrip), Rs 15 cash for 2024; about 24% of group profit.
NAV: group Rs 554.63 per share at 30 September 2026 (bank Rs 500.83). Voting share at 0.72x, non-voting at 0.62x.

Required return
Cost of equity 16.5% (bear 18.0%, bull 15.0%) = risk-free 8.24% + beta 0.80 × (4.2% mature-market premium + 6.08% country premium). Beta 0.80 is the higher of Damodaran's money-center bank beta (0.70) and the median of three local betas (0.65, 0.80, 0.84), all from web-search extracts, so it is provisional until January. No WACC: a bank's debt is its raw material.

Valuation (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified price to book | 341.3 | 475.4 | 693.3 | 478.8
P/E method | 333.0 | 462.0 | 598.0 | 450.5
Dividend model | 264.4 | 410.8 | 657.4 | 416.2
Residual income | 276.0 | 436.0 | 730.8 | 447.0
Average | 303.7 | 446.1 | 669.9 | 448
Fair value Rs 448 (weights 30/50/20, about 0.81x group NAV), buy price Rs 381 (15% below), strong buy Rs 336 (25% below).

Assumptions
Cost of equity 18.0% / 16.5% / 15.0%; long-run group ROE 13% / 15% / 17% (one point lower than before); ROE path 13% flat / 14.5%→15% / 16%→17%; profit growth for five years 6% / 9% / 12%; long-run growth 5% / 6% / 7%; 2027 EPS Rs 74 / 84 / 92 at 4.5x / 5.5x / 6.5x; payout 24%, rising to 62% / 60% / 59% after five years.
Growth check: share of profit kept × ROE (76% × 16.9% for 2025) supports 12.8% a year; every scenario is at or below it. Long-run growth stays under the 12.24% bond yield and needs 38–41% of profit kept. Earnings run-rate: the base Rs 84 is about level with the Rs 81–83 trailing figure; the bear Rs 74 is 9–11% below it, because the trailing year includes Q4 2025's write-back.

Voting or non-voting?
Both classes get the same dividends and the same share of profit; only the voting share has a vote. The non-voting share at Rs 346.25 is 13% cheaper and below the buy price, so for a long-term investor buying 500 shares it is the better buy.

Buy plan (500 shares)
200 at up to Rs 381, 150 at up to Rs 360, 150 at up to Rs 336: average about Rs 361, total about Rs 180,600.
The non-voting share at Rs 346.25 already meets the first two tiers; the third needs a 3% fall, and it traded at Rs 314.50 in Q3. The voting share needs about a 5% fall for the first tier (its 2026 low was Rs 377.00) and about 16% for the strong-buy price, which it hasn't touched in 2026.

What would change my view
Higher: group ROE back above 15% with provisions at a normal level; Q4 2026 profit growing again; the margin holding near 4.5% while loans grow; a bigger cash dividend for 2026; lower interest rates.
Lower: the 20% loan growth turning into bad loans in 2027–2028; capital falling further, leading to more scrip dividends or a rights issue; more trading losses not offset by exchange gains; higher bank taxes; deposit costs rising faster than loan rates.

Business tests: 4 of 4 passed (return on equity, capital, steady profit, dividends), so HNB is still a good business, but two are getting thinner: the bank's ROE (15.7%) is only just above 15% and the group's (13.9%) is below, and capital headroom has shrunk to about 3 points of total capital. Category: buy now (the non-voting share is below the buy price), up from watch list.
